acceptance-criteria.criterion: When a link is posted with a url and a title, the system shall store it and return 201 with an integer id, the submitted url and title, and a created_at timestamp.
When a link is posted with a url and no title, the system shall store it with a null title and return 201.
If a link is posted with no url field, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.

context.data-model: Link(id integer pk, url text not null, title text null, created_at timestamp not null)
context.prd-excerpt:
Feature "Save a link" (save-link, must-have).
User story: As someone collecting links, I want to store a URL with an optional title, so that I can come back to it without keeping a browser tab open.
Description: A POST endpoint that accepts a URL and an optional title, stores it, and returns the stored record including its generated id and creation timestamp.
The URL is the only required field. If no title is supplied the field is stored as null rather than being derived from the page, because fetching the page would make the endpoint depend on the network.
Considerations (save-link): Duplicate URLs are allowed. Deduplication sounds obviously desirable but needs a rule for what to do with the existing record's tags and timestamp, and that decision is not worth making for a fixture. This is an implementation constraint carried from the feature's <notes><considerations>, not an acceptance criterion - it has no criterion id and must not be given one. Its practical effect on this task: DO NOT put a unique constraint or unique index on `url`.

requirements.requirement:
Create file `app/models/link.py` defining exactly one model class, `Link`:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from sqlalchemy import DateTime, Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.db import Base
def _utcnow_naive() -> datetime: """Current UTC time, as a naive datetime matching the DateTime column.""" return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
class Link(Base): """A saved link. Owned by the save-link feature."""
__tablename__ = "links"
id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) url: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False) title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True, default=None) created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DateTime, nullable=False, default=_utcnow_naive )
The table name is exactly `links`. L3-004's handler and L4-003's foreign key are both written against that string.

`created_at` must use a PYTHON-side default (`default=_utcnow_naive`), not a database-side one. Do NOT use `server_default=func.now()`.
The reason is list-links#2, "The system shall order listed links most recently created first". SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP has one-second resolution, so several links created inside one test would share a timestamp and the ordering guarantee would be untestable. `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` has microsecond resolution.
The default must produce a NAIVE datetime (`.replace(tzinfo=None)`) to match the `DateTime` column, which is timezone-naive. This is not cosmetic: L3-004's tests construct links with explicit naive values such as `datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)`, and mixing naive and aware datetimes in one column raises `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` on comparison. Storing UTC while declaring the column naive is the deliberate choice; do not use `DateTime(timezone=True)`.
`created_at` must remain assignable by the caller. Passing `created_at=` explicitly to the constructor must override the default - which is what a `default=` callable does and a `server_default` does not.

Replace the contents of `app/models/__init__.py` with:
"""SQLAlchemy models.
Importing this package registers every model on Base.metadata, which is what makes Base.metadata.create_all create the tables. app/db.py's init_db() imports this package for exactly that reason. """
from app.models.link import Link
__all__ = ["Link"]
L4-003 extends this file with Tag and LinkTag. Do not pre-import them here - those modules do not exist yet and the import would fail.

Do NOT add a unique constraint or unique index on `url`. save-link's considerations state that duplicate URLs are allowed, and a unique constraint would turn a permitted second save of the same URL into an IntegrityError.

Do NOT define a `tags` relationship, a `Tag` model, a `LinkTag` model, or any `relationship()` on Link. Tag and LinkTag are L4-003's, and the analysis pass records that tag-links "adds no column to Link". L3-004 joins through LinkTag explicitly with `select(Link).join(LinkTag, ...).join(Tag, ...)` and needs no ORM relationship attribute.
Do NOT modify app/db.py, app/main.py, app/api/links.py or app/schemas/link.py, and do not edit any test file created by layer 3.

This file must NOT use a `db_session` or `client` fixture - tests/conftest.py is created by L4-004, which depends on this task. Build a per-test engine and session with a module-level pytest fixture inside this file:
from datetime import datetime
import pytest from sqlalchemy import create_engine, inspect, text from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker
from app.db import Base from app.models import Link
@pytest.fixture(name="session") def session_fixture(tmp_path): engine = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'test.db'}") Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) factory = sessionmaker(bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False) with factory() as session: yield session engine.dispose()
Import `Link` from `app.models` (the package), not from `app.models.link`, so that this file also proves requirement 3's export.
Test: test_stores_a_link_with_a_url_and_a_title_and_reads_it_back - `link = Link(url="https://example.com/article", title="An article")` - `session.add(link); session.commit()` - Assert `isinstance(link.id, int)` and `link.id > 0` - the integer id of save-link#1 - Assert `link.url == "https://example.com/article"` - Assert `link.title == "An article"` - Assert `isinstance(link.created_at, datetime)` - the created_at timestamp of save-link#1 - Assert `link.created_at.tzinfo is None` - naive, per requirement 2 - Re-read from a second session on the same engine and assert all four values survive the round trip unchanged - This is the STORAGE half of save-link#1 ("the system shall store it ... with an integer id, the submitted url and title, and a created_at timestamp"). The 201 response half is asserted by L3-003 in tests/test_save_link.py. - Pattern event-driven: one action (storing a link with both fields) produces one observable outcome (the row reads back with an id, both values and a timestamp).
Test: test_stores_a_link_with_no_title_as_null - `link = Link(url="https://example.com/untitled")` - title omitted entirely - `session.add(link); session.commit()` - Assert `link.title is None` - stored as null, not as an empty string and not derived - Re-read from a second session and assert `reloaded.title is None` - Assert the stored value really is SQL NULL, not the string "None": `session.execute(text("SELECT title FROM links WHERE id = :i"), {"i": link.id}).scalar() is None` - This is the STORAGE half of save-link#2. The 201 response half is asserted by L3-003. - Pattern event-driven: one action (storing a link without a title) produces one observable outcome (a null title).
Test: test_a_link_with_no_url_cannot_be_stored - `session.add(Link(title="no url here"))` - `with pytest.raises(IntegrityError): session.commit()` - `session.rollback()` - Assert `session.query(Link).count() == 0` - nothing was stored - This is the STORAGE half of save-link#3, "and store nothing": the NOT NULL constraint on `url` means a urlless link can never reach the table even if validation were bypassed. The "return 422" half is asserted by L3-001 (LinkCreate rejects the payload) and L3-003 (the endpoint returns 422). - Pattern unwanted-behaviour: this is the error path stated by the criterion itself - the thing that must NOT happen (a urlless link being stored) does not happen. The failure case is read off the criterion, not invented.
Test: test_duplicate_urls_are_allowed - Store `Link(url="https://example.com/same", title="first")` and commit - Store `Link(url="https://example.com/same", title="second")` and commit - Assert `session.query(Link).count() == 2` - Assert the two rows have different `id` values - Asserts requirement 4. Cites NO acceptance criterion: "Duplicate URLs are allowed" comes from save-link's <notes><considerations> and was deliberately not promoted to a criterion by the analysis pass. It is asserted here as an implementation constraint.
Test: test_created_at_default_is_applied_and_is_overridable - Store `Link(url="https://example.com/auto")` with no created_at; assert `link.created_at is not None` - Store `Link(url="https://example.com/explicit", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0))` - Assert `explicit.created_at == datetime(2026, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)` after commit and re-read - the caller's value was NOT overwritten by the default - Store two links in immediate succession with no created_at and assert their `created_at` values differ, proving sub-second resolution - Asserts requirement 2. Cites no acceptance criterion directly; it protects list-links#2, which L3-004 asserts.
Test: test_links_table_shape_matches_the_declared_data_model - `columns = {c["name"]: c for c in inspect(session.get_bind()).get_columns("links")}` - Assert `set(columns) == {"id", "url", "title", "created_at"}` - exactly four columns, no extras invented and none of tag-links' columns leaked in (requirement 5) - Assert `columns["url"]["nullable"] is False` - Assert `columns["title"]["nullable"] is True` - Assert `columns["created_at"]["nullable"] is False` - Assert `inspect(session.get_bind()).get_pk_constraint("links")["constrained_columns"] == ["id"]` - Assert `inspect(session.get_bind()).get_indexes("links") == []` and that no unique constraint exists on url (requirement 4) - Assert `Link.__tablename__ == "links"` - Asserts the <data-model> block carried above, verbatim from save-link's notes.
Test: test_link_is_exported_from_the_models_package - `import app.models` - Assert `app.models.Link is Link` - Assert `"links" in Base.metadata.tables` after importing app.models, proving requirement 3 registers the table on the shared metadata that init_db() relies on - Asserts requirement 3.
